them for elimination by the liver. Zinc, an important cofactor in RNA and DNA synthesis, is released from peripheral tissues by inﬂam-
matory cytokines, incorporated into the zinc transporting protein metallothionein in liver andkidney, and subsequently utilized by the
immune system. Fever and loss of appetite (anorexia) often occur as a result of increased pro-inﬂammatory cytokine production due to
a direct action of these cytokines on the hypothalamus. Pro-inﬂammatory cytokines also modify metabolism in the liver. Large
increases in the rates of gluconeogenesis, glycogen breakdown, and urea synthesis occur. Blood glucose, urea, and triacylglycerol
